title: The Dog in the Manger
text:
A dog was looking for a comfortable place to sleep and found one in the stable, lying in the manger on the soft hay that had been put there for the cattle.

In the evening an ox came in from a long day of work in the fields, tired and hungry, and went to the manger to eat. The dog woke up, jumped to its feet and snarled. Every time the ox came close, the dog barked and snapped at its nose, so that the poor animal could not take a single mouthful.

The dog had no use for the hay. It could not eat it, and it did not even need to sleep there; the stable had other corners. Yet it would not let the ox have what the ox needed.

At last the ox gave up and turned away. "What a spiteful creature," it said. "It cannot eat the hay itself, and it will not let those eat it who can."
lesson: Notice when you are holding on to something only so that someone else cannot have it. Letting go of what you do not need costs you nothing and earns goodwill.
caveat: The fable is attributed to Aesop by tradition but appears only in later collections, not in the oldest Greek ones.
